title: Repeated register addition run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean-valued oracle on four indices and finite Boolean strings, and let $x$ be a Boolean string. Choose a phase $q$ among the first search, second search, and final scan, natural numbers $j,i$ with $i<K_0$ and $K_0-i=j$, a machine state $S$, and memory contents $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose the width register of $S$ is $i$ times its width factor, its scratch register is zero, every register is at most $B$, and $K_0$ times its width factor is at most $B$. From the configuration at copy-loop stage $0$ for index $i$ and phase $q$, with registers $S$, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$, the machine reaches the instruction to clear the width register with that register equal to $K_0$ times the original width factor, all other registers unchanged, memory still $M$, and memory head still at $0$; at every step strictly before the endpoint, the register side conditions hold, every register is at most $B$, and the memory head lies between $0$ and $P$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{orc}$ is a Boolean oracle on four indices and finite Boolean strings
$q$ is one of the first search, second search, or final scan phases
The width register of $S$ equals $i$ times its width factor
The scratch register of $S$ is zero
Every register of $S$ is at most $B$
$K_0$ times the width factor of $S$ is at most $B$
$M$ is memory contents, a map from integers to Booleans
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathcal{O}$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four
indices and each finite bit string, and fix an input bit string $x$. Choose a phase $q$
from the first search, second search, and final scan, and natural numbers $j,i$ with
$i<K_0$ and $K_0-i=j$. Let $S$ be a register state whose word-width register is $iS.X$,
whose scratch register is $0$, whose registers are all at most $B$, and for which
$K_0S.X\le B$; let $M$ be any memory contents. Starting with the multiplication loop at
phase $q$, index $i$, and loop stage $0$, with registers $S$, memory $M$, and head
position $0$, the machine reaches the state at the instruction to clear the width
register, with the width register changed to $K_0S.X$ and every other register
unchanged, while memory remains $M$ and the head remains at $0$. At every earlier step
of this run, all registers are at most $B$, the active deterministic instruction
satisfies its register side conditions, and the head position lies between $0$ and $P$,
inclusive.
